app.Response.description: The Response struct is used for wrapping the API response with a code, message, and data.

code.description:
Code is the HTTP status code or a custom code used to indicate the result of the request
@example 200

data.description:
Data is the response data (can be any object or null)
@example {"id": 1, "name": "John Doe"}

msg.description:
Msg is the message that describes the result of the request
@example "Request successful"

label.description: Name of the fact, for example `Founded`.

value.description: Value of the fact, for example `2015`.

height.description: Image height as Bing reports it.

position.description: Rank of the image across all result pages, starting at 1.

source.description: Site the image comes from, for example `example.com`.

source_url.description: URL of the page that hosts the image.

thumbnail.description: URL of the image thumbnail served by Bing.

title.description: Image title as shown on the Bing results page.

url.description: URL Bing links the image result to.

width.description: Image width as Bing reports it.

age.description: How long ago the article was published, as Bing shows it.

age_timestamp.description: Publication time of the article as Unix seconds in UTC. Omitted when it cannot be worked out from `age`.

description.description: Article snippet as shown on the Bing results page.
description.example: OpenAI announced a new model release.

position.description: Rank of the article in the news block, starting at 1.

related_count.description: Number of additional relevant news articles Bing groups with this story.

source.description: Name of the publication, for example `Reuters`.

title.description: Article headline as shown on the Bing results page.

attributes.description: Key facts Bing lists in the knowledge panel.

description.description: Description text shown in the knowledge panel.
description.example: OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company.

image.description: URL of the knowledge panel image.

subtitle.description: Short descriptor shown under the knowledge panel title.

title.description: Name of the entity in the knowledge panel.

url.description: URL of the entity's main website or source page.

count.description: Number of results requested per page.

next_page.description: Page number of the next page. Omitted when there is no next page.

page.description: Page number of this response, starting at 1.

previous_page.description: Page number of the previous page. Omitted on the first page.

context.description: Knowledge panel Bing shows for the query. Omitted when there is none.

low_confidence.description:
LowConfidence is true when Bing returned a well-formed page whose
organic results share no significant term with the query -- a known
upstream anomaly where Bing serves an unrelated SERP for certain
multi-word queries instead of a challenge page or an error. The
fields above are exactly what Bing
returned; nothing is fabricated, reordered, or filtered. Treat a true
value as a hint to double-check relevance (or retry) before trusting
the results, not as a guarantee they are wrong -- some low-confidence
responses are still perfectly good, they just didn't literally repeat
a distinctive word from the query. Omitted (false) on every ordinary
response.

news.description: News results Bing shows for the query. Omitted when there are none.

people_also_ask.description: Questions from Bing's People also ask block.

related_queries.description: Related searches Bing suggests for the query.

results.description: Organic web results in Bing's order.

videos.description: Video results Bing shows for the query. Omitted when there are none.

age.description: Date or age shown on the result, as Bing shows it. Omitted when Bing shows none.

age_timestamp.description: Time from `age` as Unix seconds in UTC. Omitted when it cannot be worked out.

description.description: Result snippet as shown on the Bing results page.
description.example: OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company.

display_url.description: URL as displayed under the result title on Bing.

favicon.description: URL of the site's favicon as Bing serves it.

hostname.description: Host name of the result URL.

position.description: Rank of the result across all pages for the query, starting at 1.

title.description: Result title as shown on the Bing results page.

query.description: Query prefix the suggestions were requested for.

suggestions.description: Search suggestions Bing returned, in order.

entity.description: Entity Bing matched to the suggestion. Only set when the request used `rich=true` and Bing recognises an entity.

position.description: Rank of the suggestion in the list, starting at 1.

age.description: When the video was published, as Bing shows it.

age_timestamp.description: Time from `age` as Unix seconds in UTC. Omitted when it cannot be worked out.

creator.description: Channel or creator that published the video.

duration.description: Video length as Bing shows it, for example `45:12`.

platform.description: Platform hosting the video, for example `YouTube`.

position.description: Rank of the video in the videos block, starting at 1.

title.description: Video title as shown on the Bing results page.

views.description: View count as Bing shows it, for example `1.2M views`.

info.description: Crawlora is a hosted web-data and SERP API: call documented REST endpoints and get normalized JSON instead of HTML to parse — across search/SERP, maps and local, e-commerce, app stores, social, media and finance. One API key; Crawlora runs the proxy rotation, headless browsers and parsing behind the scenes. Billed pay-on-success: charged only on a successful 2xx response, 1-10 credits per call, with a free tier of 2,000 credits per month and no card. A hosted MCP server (mcp.crawlora.net/mcp) exposes the same catalog as agent tools. Search endpoints accept `q` as a universal alias for whichever search-term parameter they document (`query`, `term`, `keyword`, or Amazon's `k`), so one parameter name works across the whole catalog; an explicitly supplied documented name always wins.

get.description: Returns Bing web search results for a query string, including organic results, optional context panel data, related queries, people-also-ask questions, news modules, video modules, and page-based pagination. Empty optional blocks are omitted from the JSON response. Locale defaults to country=us and lang=en-us. Returns 503 on a genuine transport failure or challenge page. Bing occasionally serves a well-formed page whose results share no significant term with the query; when every attempt hits this, the response is still returned as 200 with data.low_confidence set to true (and the X-Low-Confidence header) instead of being withheld, so callers get Bing's real answer plus an honest signal to double-check it rather than nothing. Queries that use the site: operator (for example site:gov.hu) are not supported: Bing serves a bot-verification challenge for them, so they are rejected with 400 before any request is made. Use the DuckDuckGo (/api/v1/duckduckgo/search), Brave (/api/v1/brave/search), or Yahoo (/api/v1/yahoo-search/search) search endpoints for domain-restricted searches instead.

parameters.description: Search query
parameters.name: q

parameters.description: 1-based page number; defaults to 1
parameters.name: page

parameters.description: Results per page; defaults to 10, clamped to 1..50
parameters.name: count

parameters.description: Two-letter country code; defaults to us
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: Bing UI language; defaults to en-us
parameters.name: lang

200.description: data.low_confidence is true when Bing's results shared no significant term with the query (see the field's description); the data is still exactly what Bing returned

503.description: Bing upstream request failed (transport failure, challenge page, or every hedge attempt rejected -- see data.low_confidence for the case where Bing did answer but every attempt looked unrelated to the query)

get.description: Returns Bing autosuggest query completions for a query prefix. Locale defaults to country=us and lang=en-us. Suggestions are fetched from public Bing suggest endpoints and trimmed to the requested count. `rich=true` adds entity cards (name, description, image) where Bing shows them.

parameters.description: Suggestions to return; defaults to 10, clamped to 1..12
parameters.name: count

parameters.description: Two-letter country code; defaults to us
parameters.name: country

parameters.description: Bing UI language; defaults to en-us
parameters.name: lang

parameters.description: Add entity name, description, and image to suggestions Bing resolves to a known entity; defaults to false
